gary_2026_09_11_ai_briefing_by_startup_g.title: AI Briefing By Startup Grind - Workforce Gap In AI Readiness
gary_2026_09_11_ai_briefing_by_startup_g.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_11_ai_briefing_by_startup_g.summary: Gary's Guide: The AI Briefing is a high-velocity roundtable for decision-makers brought to you by Startup Grind. We bypass the hype by dissecting one high-signal industry deck with a room of vetted founders, operators, & enterprise executives. No lectures-just a 60-minute deep-dive into the tactics & data defining your next quarter. The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise. This Month's Source: 2026 People Readiness Report (Kyndryl - Jun 2026) Kyndryl's newest survey of 1,100 business & technology leaders found something specific: workforce readiness dropped 6 points this year, to just 23%, even as broad AI deployment climbed to 57%. The gap between rollout speed & people readiness is widening. Leaders agree the technology itself isn't the constraint anymore. 79% say AI will outpace their organization's ability to adapt its workforce, governance, & operating model. And the confidence gap tracks straight down the org chart: half of executive leadership believes their teams are enthusiastic about AI, but only 3 in 10 individual contributors & entry-level employees agree. The same survey found 66% of organizations have already given AI agents unsupervised read & write access to their core systems of record. Trust & governance haven't caught up with what's already running in production. The Mission: Where adoption, the C-suite divide, & agentic governance actually meet Every AI Briefing this year has examined one piece of this from the top: how fast enterprises adopted, where leadership's confidence outran execution, & how governance is lagging behind autonomous agents. This session looks at the piece none of those touched directly: whether the workforce itself is ready, & what the data says happens to trust & outcomes when it isn't. We'll use Kyndryl's own segmentation, the small group of organizations it calls Pacesetters, to ground the conversation in what readiness actually requires versus what most organizations are doing instead. The Format: We'll open with the readiness numbers: adoption at 57%, workforce readiness at 23% & falling, & the widening distance between what executives report & what individual contributors experience. From there, the room works through Kyndryl's Pacesetter data: the 9% of organizations that redesigned roles, built change management, & got measurably better outcomes for it. What's replicable here, & what's easy to claim but hard to actually execute. We'll also spend time on the report's agentic AI numbers: two-thirds of organizations already letting agents act on core systems without a person in the loop, & what that means for a governance conversation this room started in August. Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Compare your own workforce-readiness numbers against Kyndryl's benchmark, & see what actually separates the 9% of organizations getting outcomes from the 91% still catching up. Founders & Builders: See where the readiness gap (skills visibility, change management, trust-building) is becoming a real buying trigger for enterprise customers, not just a talking point in their RFPs. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Get concrete detail on what change management & role redesign look like at organizations that have already done the work, not just the aspiration. The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring a specific example from your own org, especially anywhere the gap between leadership's read & the floor's experience showed up.

gary_2026_09_12_agents_everywhere_global.summary: Gary's Guide: Agents, Everywhere: Bots, Channels, & More - Global Hackathon A global hackathon with OpenAI On Saturday, September 12, AI Tinkerers cities around the world are joining one shared build day. Build an agent for a place people already work, talk, & live, then make it meaningfully more useful because of that context. Event details Date: Saturday, September 12, 2026 Time: 10 a.m.-5 p.m. local time Location: Shared upon acceptance Format: Focused local build day, connected to one global challenge Food & drinks: Provided The challenge Most agents still wait inside a separate chat window. This build day starts from a different premise: the most useful agents will show up inside the tools, channels, devices, & environments where people already have work to do. Build a working agent that belongs somewhere new. Your project might live: At work: Slack, Teams, email, documents, calendars, tickets, support, or live collaboration In your pocket: messaging, mobile, notifications, & short asynchronous moments On the web: browsers & software where an agent can research, navigate, transact, or take action In the room: voice, vision, wearables, robotics, & other physical-world interfaces These are examples, not separate tracks. Every team around the world enters the same global submission pool. Your build stack OpenAI & the event partners will provide shared starter materials, technical resources, & builder credits/offers where available. We will share the final starter repo & access details ahead of the event. You do not need to use every tool in the stack. Choose the resources that make your idea better & make the technical choices that fit the project. More starter materials, technical resources, sponsor offers, & event details will be added to this page as they are finalized.

jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

jc_culture_43488_2026_09_25_jersey_city_.summary: The Jersey City Poetry Festival (JCPOFEST) is an interdisciplinary, intergenerational event taking place September 25–27 under this year’s theme “Viva! Joy as Resistance.” This multi-venue celebration fuses poetry with music, dance, visual art, storytelling, and film—bringing generations, disciplines, and communities together to imagine, question, connect, and experience the radical possibility of collective JOY. Showcasing an extraordinary constellation of emerging and critically acclaimed voices, the festival features 5th U.S. Presidential Inaugural Poet Richard Blanco, the Grammy-performing Resistance Revival Chorus, and a panel with poets from Cave Canem (represented by Pulitzer Prize finalist Evie Shockley), Kundiman, and CantoMundo.
